morphology.shape: Spherical enveloped Dane particle with an icosahedral nucleocapsid core
morphology.size: ~42 nm for the complete Dane particle; smaller subviral spherical/tubular particles are also produced, ~22 nm
morphology.notes: Genome is a partially double-stranded, relaxed circular DNA — unusual among DNA viruses; replication proceeds through an RNA intermediate via reverse transcription

habitat.hostAssociation: Human pathogen; chronic carriers serve as the main reservoir
habitat.environmentalOccurrence: Can remain infectious on surfaces for extended periods outside the host, relatively stable compared to many enveloped viruses

microscopy.appearance: Electron microscopy of serum in research settings can show spherical Dane particles plus excess smaller subviral envelope-only particles

culture.media: Not routinely cultured in clinical or most research labs, historically limited by poor in vitro culture systems
culture.growthCharacteristics: Requires living hepatocytes; not grown on standard media

identificationClues: Diagnosed by serologic markers (HBsAg, anti-HBs, HBeAg, anti-HBc, anti-HBe) and HBV DNA viral load, not by culture
Partially double-stranded circular DNA genome, unusual among DNA viruses
Enveloped Dane particle with an icosahedral core (HBcAg)
Chronic infection is defined by persistence of HBsAg beyond 6 months

diseases: Hepatocellular carcinoma — a long-term complication of chronic infection
virulenceFactors: Ability to establish chronic infection via persistence in hepatocytes
Integration of viral DNA into the host genome, contributing to hepatocellular carcinoma risk
clinicalImportance.transmission: Blood and body fluids — percutaneous/mucosal exposure, perinatal transmission, and sexual contact
clinicalImportance.epidemiology: A major global cause of chronic liver disease and hepatocellular carcinoma; effective vaccination has substantially reduced incidence in many regions since its introduction
clinicalImportance.labSignificance: Serologic panels (HBsAg, anti-HBc, anti-HBs, HBeAg/anti-HBe) distinguish acute infection, chronic infection, immunity from vaccination, and past resolved infection

examFacts.shape: Enveloped Dane particle with an icosahedral core
examFacts.keyBiochemicalReaction: Not applicable — diagnosed serologically and by viral load
examFacts.importantDisease: Chronic hepatitis B; hepatocellular carcinoma risk
examFacts.importantTest: HBsAg and HBV DNA viral load; full serologic panel for infection stage
examFacts.distinguishingFeature: Partially double-stranded circular DNA genome replicating via reverse transcription, unusual for a DNA virus
